subject: Commit Corridor Remedy — proposed language + pricing exhibit question
messages:
From: VelvetHealth Procurement <procurement@velvethealth.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: sophia.lee@velvethealth.com, sue.klein@velvethealth.com
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing exhibit v3 + commit corridor questions

Marissa —

Thanks for the fast turn here. Attached is VelvetHealth's marked-up version of the Pricing Exhibit (VelvetHealth_Exhibit_Pricing_v3.docx) and a short redline (redline_commit_corridor.pdf) showing our preferred remedy for a commit shortfall in the "commit corridor" (Section 2.3). High level: we are open to a true-up but want a defined waterfall so that small shortfalls are cured via credits or carry-forward before any termination/penalty triggers.

Two concrete asks from our side:
- Can Redwood confirm whether you will accept carry-forward of credits for up to 2 quarters as an alternative to cash repayment?
- For partial shortfalls (<20% of quarterly commit), would Redwood accept a pro rata credit rather than accelerating the fee floor?

We added comments in the doc where we had uncertainty about the "floor/ceiling trigger" language and how it interacts with the annual true-up. We also attached a simple matrix (commit_corridor_matrix.xlsx) that shows three scenarios and our proposed remedial order.

Would like to get this resolved ahead of the procurement review next week. Are you available for a 30-minute call on Monday (Aug 23) 10am PT?

Attachments:
- VelvetHealth_Exhibit_Pricing_v3.docx (docx)
- redline_commit_corridor.pdf (pdf)
- commit_corridor_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)

Best,
Sue Klein
Head of Procurement, VelvetHealth
procurement@velvethealth.com

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: procurement@velvethealth.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2027 10:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit v3 + commit corridor questions

Sue —

Thanks for the clear summary and the matrix, that helps. Looping in Karthik (pricing/legal lead) and Laura (contracts) to draft suggested language and confirm commercial impact. Jonas from finance is on cc to validate the crediting flow.

Initial notes from me:
- We are generally open to a carry-forward mechanic for small, recoverable shortfalls, but we need language that caps exposure and preserves predictable unit economics for Redwood (e.g., maximum carry period and a hard cap on carried credits).
- We want the waterfall to be unambiguous: (1) automated pro rata credit applied against next invoice; (2) carry-forward up to N quarters; (3) final annual true-up (cash or one-time invoice).

Karthik/Laura — can you take the attached redline and propose explicit clause text that we can send back to VelvetHealth? Please call out any downstream billing/system constraints (Jonas, anything I should be aware of?) and estimate the implementation delta (config + legal approval).

I can confirm a Monday 10am PT call for now; will send calendar invite once we have a draft to discuss.

--
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
[Attachment: redline_commit_corridor.pdf]

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, procurement@velvethealth.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2027 16:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit v3 + commit corridor questions

Marissa / Sue —

Thanks — I reviewed VelvetHealth's redline and the matrix. Below is a proposed replacement paragraph for Section 2.3 (Commit Corridor Remedy). I flagged points where VelvetHealth's suggested carry-forward would need a limit or additional operational steps.

Proposed clause (draft):
"In the event Customer fails to meet the Quarterly Commit by more than 5% but less than or equal to 20% (a "Minor Shortfall"), Redwood will automatically apply a pro rata credit equal to the shortfall percentage against the next invoice. If the Customer remains below the Quarterly Commit for two consecutive quarters, Customer may elect to carry forward remaining credit to offset up to two subsequent quarterly invoices (Carry-Forward Period). Any unused carry-forward at the end of the Carry-Forward Period will be subject to the Annual True-Up described in Section 2.5. For shortfalls greater than 20% (a "Material Shortfall"), the parties will follow the Annual True-Up procedure, which may include cash settlement or one-time invoicing to reconcile outstanding balances and record a potential adjustment to the Fee Floor for the following year."

Operational notes:
- Jonas: implementation will require a new crediting ledger field and a two-quarter lifecycle for carry entries; estimated engineering cost: 2-3 sprints for automation, lower effort for manual credits.
- We should limit the max total carry-forward exposure to 25% of the next quarter's invoice to protect Redwood cashflow (language above can include that cap if you prefer).

Questions for VelvetHealth:
1) Is a two-quarter Carry-Forward Period acceptable?
2) Do you accept a maximum carry cap (we propose 25% of the following quarter's invoice)?
3) For Material Shortfalls, would VelvetHealth prefer a time-bound cure (e.g., 30 days) before the Annual True-Up steps are invoked?

I'll turn this into a marked-up doc tonight and upload; Marissa, happy to lead the call on Monday.

- Karthik
Director, Pricing & Contracts, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: commit_corridor_matrix.xlsx]

From: Sophia Lee <sophia.lee@velvethealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: sue.klein@velvethealth.com
Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2027 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit v3 + commit corridor questions

Karthik / Marissa —

Thanks for the draft clause. Overall VelvetHealth is comfortable with the structure but we have two items we cannot accept as written: the proposed 25% cap on carry-forward exposure and the automatic pro rata application without a short notice window. Our counter-proposal below aims to balance operational predictability with customer protections.

VelvetHealth counter-proposals: 
- Carry-Forward Period: we agree to a two-quarter carry-forward window, but request that the aggregate carry-forward cap be expressed as a percentage of the Quarterly Commit (we propose 40% of Quarterly Commit rather than a percentage of the next invoice). This aligns with our budgeting process.
- Shortfall remediation timing: for Minor Shortfalls (<20%), we request a 30-day cure window before any automated credit is applied, to allow for usage reconciliation and dispute resolution. If no dispute is raised within 30 days, the pro rata credit may be applied to the next invoice.

On Material Shortfalls (>20%), we accept the Annual True-Up framework but ask for explicit language allowing the Customer to request a one-time remediation plan (e.g., increased usage to offset shortfall) in lieu of immediate cash settlement, subject to Redwood's reasonable approval.

If you can accept the two points above, VelvetHealth is willing to move this to signature. We can take the redline you send and produce a clean markup for signature-ready review.

Best regards,
Sophia Lee
Senior Counsel, VelvetHealth
sophia.lee@velvethealth.com
